facts.statement: Written consent from the student (or parent, if the student is under 18) is required before disclosing education records; the platform must offer an annual opt-out for directory information.
facts.source_title: FERPA Compliance in 2026: A Guide for University Cybersecurity Leaders

facts.statement: Any third-party vendor or integration handling student data must operate under a signed FERPA-compliant data agreement, and the platform must log every access to a student's education record.
facts.source_title: What FERPA Actually Requires of an Edtech Platform

facts.statement: Students must gain direct access rights to their own education records once they turn 18 or enrol at the postsecondary level (FERPA's transfer of rights from parent to student).
facts.source_title: Student Data Privacy & FERPA Guide: School Records Rights (2026)

facts.statement: Course content and the platform UI should conform to WCAG 2.1/2.2 Level AA, matching the accessibility bar the DOJ's Title II digital-accessibility rule sets for public higher-education institutions.
facts.source_title: Title II Video Accessibility: What WCAG 2.1 AA Requires

facts.statement: All instructional video must carry accurate, synchronised closed captions with speaker identification — burned-in captions don't qualify, and auto-generated captions must be edited for accuracy rather than relied on alone.
facts.source_title: Video Captioning Requirements: WCAG 2.2 Media Accessibility Compliance

facts.statement: Course content should be exportable in a standard interoperable format (SCORM and/or xAPI) so it is not locked into a single LMS.
facts.source_title: E-Learning Standards: A Comprehensive Guide to SCORM, xAPI, CMI5, and Modern LMS Compliance
